truths.truth: A config naming only roles.cad-planner.{model,effort} makes `route.mjs resolve --role cad-planner` return that model, that effort, and the agent file RUNG_FILES maps that rung to.
truths.evidence: Live run against a scratch config `{"roles":{"cad-planner":{"model":"haiku","effort":"low"}}}` (CADENCE_GLOBAL_CONFIG pointed at an empty layer) returned model=haiku, effort=low, agent=cad-planner-low, pinned=false, model_source=roles.cad-planner.model, with reason entries 'roles.cad-planner.effort: high -> low' and 'roles.cad-planner.model: opus -> haiku'. cad-planner-low is exactly RUNG_FILES['cad-planner'].low (cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs:38-44). Wiring traced end to end: rolesIn(c) reads the block at route.mjs:364-367 into readConfig's `roles` field (route.mjs:280), roleEntryIn (route.mjs:375-378) narrows it to this role at route.mjs:1030, the rung arm consumes it at route.mjs:1047-1113 and the model arm at route.mjs:1404-1445. Named test `a roles-block model and rung resolve together, and pinned stays FALSE` and `a roles-block start rung replaces the cell's, and picks that rung's file` both pass.

truths.truth: A config carrying only `stakes` and no roles block resolves exactly what it resolved before the phase, across all eighteen (level, role) cells.
truths.evidence: Direct pre-phase-vs-now comparison, not just the in-repo fixture: exported cadence-core at e4ec3976 (the parent of the first phase commit a504d234) with `git archive` into a scratch tree and ran both route.mjs binaries over a stakes-only config for all 18 (level, role) cells at --attempt 1 and --attempt 2 (36 envelopes). After dropping the new `model_source` key the JSON was byte-identical in all 36; differing: 0. Negative control on the same harness: the same comparison on a config that DOES set roles.cad-executor.{model,effort} differs as expected (old: opus/high/cad-executor, new: haiku/low/cad-executor-low), so the harness is not blind. In-repo proof also present and passing: 18 `stakes-only fallback <level>/<role>` cases at cadence-core/bin/route.test.mjs:149-162, each asserting `'roles' in written === false` on the fixture file's own parsed contents plus model/effort/agent/model_source against the hand-written CELLS rows at :89-110. `node --test --test-name-pattern='stakes-only fallback'` -> 18 pass, 0 fail.

truths.truth: A roles.<role>.model outside the four aliases resolves ok:true with the routed cell's model, a warnings[] entry naming the rejected string, and never falls through to model.overrides.<role>.
truths.evidence: Live: `{"roles":{"cad-verifier":{"model":"gpt-5-turbo"}}}` -> ok:true, model=opus (the shipped/cad-verifier cell), model_source=cell, pinned=false, warnings=['roles.cad-verifier.model="gpt-5-turbo" is not a known alias (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable); routed opus stands']. Live with a pin also set (model.overrides.cad-verifier="opus") -> still model_source=cell and pinned=false, so the rejected string did not hand the role back to the pin. Code: route.mjs:1410-1430 - the roles branch is entered on presence, and its else arm warns and leaves `model` and `modelSource` untouched, so the `else if (pin != null)` arm at :1431 is unreachable once the roles key is set. Named tests `a roles model outside the aliases warns, and the routed cell model stands` and `a rejected roles model does NOT fall through to the pin` pass. Cosmetic note (already disclosed in SUMMARY 'Open items' and adjudicated `survived`/low in .planning/phases/2/ADJUDICATION-diff-plan-1.json): the pin-conflict warning at route.mjs:1416 says the roles key 'decides this role's model' before the alias is validated, so on a rejected string it precedes the correcting warning one line later. Both warnings were observed in the same envelope; the resolved values are correct.

truths.truth: Setting both roles.<role>.effort and model.effort.<role> resolves the roles value and emits a warnings[] entry naming which key won.
truths.evidence: Live: `{"roles":{"cad-planner":{"effort":"max"}},"model":{"effort":{"cad-planner":"low"}}}` -> effort=max, agent=cad-planner-max, warnings=['roles.cad-planner.effort="max" (config) wins over model.effort.cad-planner="low", which names the same rung one key out; the roles block decides'], reason='roles.cad-planner.effort: high -> max (config, wins over the shipped/cad-planner cell)'. Code: route.mjs:1047-1058 selects `wanted` and `effortKey` from the roles entry when set and warns when both are, and `effortKey` is what is interpolated into all four rung arms (:1069, :1072, :1094, :1107) and both retry reasons (:1161, :1171). Named test `the roles block WINS over model.effort, and a warning names the winner` passes; `a roles entry that is not a map contributes nothing, and the older key answers` pins the defensive read.

truths.truth: A raised risk floor clamps a below-floor roles.<role>.effort, and `reason` names the raise, the surface and the key that pinned the rung.
truths.evidence: Live, built fresh rather than reusing the test fixture: a scratch repo whose .planning/phases/3/PLAN-1.md declares src/load.mjs, that file carrying a credential-named assignment, config `{"roles":{"cad-plan-checker":{"effort":"low"}}}` with the surface question answered. `resolve --role cad-plan-checker --phase 3` -> stakes=shipped, effort=medium (the raised cell's rung, not the pinned low), agent=cad-plan-checker-medium, reason carries 'risk floor: phase 3: src/load.mjs touches secrets ...; level solo -> shipped' and 'roles.cad-plan-checker.effort="low" does not apply: src/load.mjs touches secrets, and the raised shipped/cad-plan-checker cell's "medium" rung is the floor'. Clamp terms unchanged per D-04: still gated on floor.raised at route.mjs:1090 and still compared through rung_order. Named test `clamp: a raised level floors a ROLES-block rung too, and names THAT key` passes, and the three sibling clamp cases (discounted phase, waived surface, torn rung_order) still pass in the full run.

truths.truth: All twelve roles keys are reachable through config.mjs get/set, and self-verify reports ok:true with no missing-reach-row, inert-config-key or unknown-config-key.
truths.evidence: `config.mjs keys` lists exactly 12 keys under the `roles.` prefix (six .model, six .effort). One `config.mjs get` naming all twelve -> ok:true with null for each. One `config.mjs set` writing all twelve -> ok:true with 12 `changed` entries and a well-formed nested roles block on disk; `set roles.cad-executor.effort=ludicrous` -> ok:false naming 'must be one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, null'. `node cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs` -> ok:true, problems: 0, empty code set, with config-keys, config-reach, effort-enums and budgets all in the checked list. Reach rows present one per key at cadence-core/references/config-reach.md:120-131. The reverse arm is live, not just quiet: the drift guard was exercised against the shipped schema through the real lib (effortEnumIssues from cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs:330, called from self-verify.mjs:1202) - shipped schema returns [], a roles enum with xhigh removed returns effort-enum-drift naming roles.cad-verifier.effort, an added roles.cad-nobody.effort returns unknown-effort-role, and a deleted roles.cad-executor.effort returns missing-effort-key. Named tests `check 1: roles.<role>.effort prose covers every role, and its absence is inert` and `placeholder keys expand: <t> prose covers every trigger key` pass.

truths.truth: The roles block carries exactly `model` and `effort` per role - a third field is an unknown key.
truths.evidence: `config.mjs validate --file <scratch>` on `{"roles":{"cad-planner":{"model":"opus","effort":"low","retry":"max"}}}` -> ok:false, checked:3, errors:[{"key":"roles.cad-planner.retry","error":"unknown key"}]. The two legitimate leaves validated clean in the same call, so the refusal is scoped to the third field and not to the block. cadence-core/config.schema.json carries twelve roles rows and no retry row; nothing in route.mjs reads a roles `retry` (roleEntryIn's consumers are only `.effort` at route.mjs:1047 and `.model` at :1407).

truths.truth: Every resolved dispatch envelope carries model_source naming the key that decided - roles.<role>.model, model.overrides.<role>, or cell.
truths.evidence: All three values observed live off one config in one run: cad-planner -> model_source='cell' (nothing set), cad-verifier -> 'model.overrides.cad-verifier' with pinned=true, cad-executor -> 'roles.cad-executor.model' with pinned=false, cad-reviewer (roles model 'nope', rejected) -> 'cell'. Presence is unconditional: resolve has exactly three `out(` exits - route.mjs:936 (unknown-role) and :1008 (unresolved), neither of which carries a `model` at all, and :1501, the single ok:true envelope, which spells `model_source: modelSource` inline with no conditional spread. The unknown-role arm was exercised live and returns no model and no model_source, which is the coherent shape. `pinned` keeps its old meaning and stays false on every roles-decided dispatch, so the announcement rule at cadence-core/references/seam-spawn-agent.md:327-333 is untouched; the new **Per-role model** bullet at :316-326 tells a caller to read model_source instead. The eighteen fallback cases each assert model_source==='cell' (route.test.mjs:160).

Read path traced: route.mjs:364-367 -> :280 -> :375-378 -> :1030 -> :1047 (rung) and :1407 (model). Named tests pass.

passes.name: model_source names the key that decided

Unconditional on the single ok:true exit at route.mjs:1501; the two ok:false exits (:936, :1008) carry no model either. pinned stays false on roles-decided dispatches, so the seam's pin-announcement rule (seam-spawn-agent.md:327-333) is unchanged.
